Haah's code FTH induces a duality of transverse-field generalized Ising models (TFGIMs). The two examples illustrate at least a part of type-I fracton (X-cube) and a part of type-II fracton (Haah's code) models can be used to construct FTH sandwiches. Moreover, we construct an explicit Sequential Quantum Circuit (SQC) switching the top boundary of X-cube sandwich, realizing the TFPIM version KW duality.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Tao Hu, Jie-Yu Zhang, Peng Ye

item.title: Lattice Configuration Generation with a Self-Learning Diffusion Model
item.description: arXiv:2607.12587v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a diffusion model for lattice field theory can be trained by self-learning, without configurations from a separate simulation, and used as the generator of an exact Markov chain. Training starts from exact samples at $\beta=0$, and along a ladder of couplings the model's own chain at each coupling, weighted by the action difference, trains the score at the next. A Metropolis-Hastings test on each proposal and its noising path keeps the sampled distribution exact for any network, so that network errors affect only the acceptance and autocorrelation times. In the two-dimensional compact XY model up to $\beta=1$, on the high-temperature side of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, ladders at $L=4$ and $8$ reproduce exact and reference values of the energy density and helicity modulus at every coupling, and the generator trained from $\beta=0$ at $L=8$ has the same acceptance as one trained on an exact chain at $\beta=1$. The acceptance follows the relation known from hybrid Monte Carlo, with terms set by the number of noise levels and by the network error per site, and a network trained at $L=4$ generates up to $L=16$ when the number of levels grows with the volume.
item.dc:creator: Akio Tomiya

item.title: Exact pair density wave in topological moire flat bands and universal superfluid stiffness
item.description:
arXiv:2608.26245v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pair-density waves (PDWs) are unconventional superconducting states beyond the BCS paradigm, but identifying them unambiguously in microscopic lattice models is generally challenging due to various competing orders. In particular, an exact realization of PDW in interacting models with topological bands remains elusive. Here we construct an interacting model on a twisted bilayer checkerboard lattice (TBCB) featuring topological flat bands, and rigorously show that an exact PDW ground state can be induced by quantum geometric nesting (QGN), owing to its momentum-space nonsymmorphic symmetry. We further prove that the superfluid stiffness of any nondegenerate QGN superconductor (including the PDW studied here and uniform superconductor) obeys the universal relation $D_s=2N_{m flat}
u(1-
u)m_{m pair}^{-1}$, where $N_{m flat}$, $
u$, and $m_{m pair}$ are the number of flat bands, flat band filling, and the two-particle effective mass, respectively. Our results reveal a rich interplay among PDW order, quantum geometry, and band topology.
item.dc:creator: Zhengzhi Wu, Ming-rui Li, Hong Yao

item.title: Stripe-Like Superconducting Enhancement and Coexisting Magnetic Texture in an Infinite Layer Nickelate
item.description: arXiv:2609.15958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Despite their promise as structural and electronic analogs to cuprates, nickelate thin films consistently exhibit broadened superconducting transitions in many experiments that remain poorly understood. Local measurements are ideal for revealing the presence of defects or competing phases, which may cause this transition broadening through a phase-separation. Here, we use scanning SQUID microscopy to investigate local superfluid density and magnetic texture of optimally doped $\mathrm{Nd}_{1-x}\mathrm{Eu}_{x}\mathrm{NiO}_{2}$ (NENO) (x=0.25) grown via molecular beam epitaxy. We observed a weakly-magnetic texture coexisting with superconductivity. Spatially resolved susceptibility imaging reveals a highly non-uniform superconducting state, characterized by a robust stripe-like enhancement pattern appearing near the phase transition. By resolving the mesoscopic landscape of electronic and magnetic inhomogeneities, these findings suggest that a competing magnetic phase is a primary contributor to the unusually broad superconducting transitions of these optimally doped NENO samples. Understanding the uncovered superconducting enhancement may provide a path to raising superconducting temperatures in these materials.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Laing, Dung Vu, Jacob Pfund, Wenzheng Wei, Frederick J. Walker, Haiyan Tan, Pavel Volkov, Rodrigo Castillo-Garza, Menka Jain, Charles Ahn, Ilya Sochnikov

item.title: Finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions
item.description: arXiv:2609.37032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with coexistent $s$- and $p$-wave interactions, regularized in the relative momentum of each pair so that they remain Galilean invariant. Pauli blocking alone then makes the trimer dispersion deviate from free center-of-mass motion, so the trimer energy can be lowest at finite total momentum. Allowing this motion expands the $abb$ region among pairs and trimers and removes the region where an odd-wave pair is lowest. The $aabb$ quartet lies below all these branches at every sampled coupling, and in a strip starting on the crossing of the two dimer-pair channels its lowest breakup channel is a moving $abb$ trimer and an atom. At weak interspecies attraction, a variational bound shows that two odd-wave Cooper pairs bind into a quartet, whose binding exceeds that of the coexisting trimer by orders of magnitude as the attraction weakens. At stronger interspecies attraction, the quartet binding relative to two unlike-species dimers disappears when the odd-wave interaction is switched off, although the even-wave interaction dominates the interaction energy. Relative to the in-vacuum case, the Fermi sea enhances the weak-coupling quartet binding, and at fixed scattering lengths the quartet binding grows with density while the coexisting trimer becomes much shallower. These results show that neither the most strongly bound pair nor the dominant interaction energy alone determines whether the quartet binds.
item.dc:creator: Yixin Guo

item.title: Energy- and momentum-resolved Cooper-pair emission from a cuprate superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2611.09857v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Superconductivity arises from Cooper pairing, but conventional photoemission probes electrons individually rather than as pairs. Here we report the observation of Cooper-pair emission from an optimally doped cuprate superconductor using two-electron angle-resolved photoemission (2e-ARPES). Below the superconducting transition, we observe a distinct two-electron emission peak at zero pair binding energy and zero pair momentum that disappears in the normal state, revealing the characteristic fingerprint of a Cooper pair. Unexpectedly, the joint energy distribution broadens markedly along the relative-energy axis as temperature decreases, while the total energy width remains nearly unchanged. This anomalous behavior cannot be explained by instrumental resolution, static disorder or thermal broadening, and instead points to scattering processes involving collective excitations of the superconductor. Our results establish 2e-ARPES as a probe of both Cooper-pair emission and the many-body dynamics of the superconducting state.
item.dc:creator: Henry Amir, Jack Zwettler, Ka Ho Wong, Genda Gu, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jorge Noronha, Dirk K. Morr, Fahad Mahmood

item.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.26587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy. Importantly, this improved accuracy requires neither further energy minimization nor increased model complexity, but rather exploits the effect of randomization on quantum states. We demonstrate dynamical averaging on non-integrable spin models, where it accelerates convergence and substantially reduces errors in observables.
item.dc:creator: John M. Martyn, Rod Rofougaran, Samuel Stein, Di Luo
